findings.title: Neither rounding assertion can distinguish Math.round from Math.floor — the cost-reconciliation rounding contract is unpinned
findings.arbiter_reasoning: Mutant: `Math.round(input.totalCostUsd * 100)` -> `Math.floor(...)`. Both tests that assert the booked cents use totalCostUsd 0.0342 (= 3.42c), where round and floor agree, so both pass unchanged (inventory rt-024, rt-025). The line is executed by both (they assert the value it produces), so this is not an unexecuted branch; and the mutant is provably NOT equivalent — 0.0355 USD books 4c under round and 3c under floor. The branch itself calls the rounding a contract: docs/directory/worker-jobs-c.md states `finalizeOnboardingDemoSpend` 'books Math.round(totalCostUsd * 100)', and both test comments say 'rounds to whole cents' / '0.0342 USD rounds to 3 cents'. The consequence is not cosmetic: finalizeOnboardingDemoCost applies `actual - RESERVATION_CENTS` to the shared daily Redis counter, so a systematic under-round biases the onboarding-demo daily budget low by up to 1c per demo, and it is the counter the 50/90/100 percent Sentry thresholds read. Fix is one fixture: use a totalCostUsd whose half-cent boundary separates the two (e.g. 0.0355 -> 4), or add a second case.
findings.reason: CLOSED in 0cf768372. Re-measured at HEAD: Math.floor, Math.trunc and Math.ceil each now FAIL `finalizeOnboardingDemoSpend swallows and logs a finalize failure` (inventory rt-065/066/067), because the test carries a 3.55c half (kills floor/trunc) and a 3.42c half (kills ceil). Math.floor also fails the worker-root success test (rt-068). The rounding contract now admits only Math.round.

findings.title: Nothing pins that cost finalization runs — and completes — before the threshold check, though the threshold check reads the counter finalization moves
findings.arbiter_reasoning: Two mutants survive the whole changed test surface (inventory rt-030, rt-031): swapping the `finalizeOnboardingDemoSpend` / `reportOnboardingDemoCostThresholds` blocks, and replacing the `await` on the first with `void`. Both execute in the covering test and neither is equivalent. `checkCostThreshold` reads `cost:onboarding-demo:<date>` (src/lib/costs/onboarding-demo-cost-guard.ts:124-125) and `finalizeOnboardingDemoCost` incrby's a negative delta on that same key (src/lib/costs/onboarding-demo-cost-guard.ts:92-94), so either mutant makes every demo evaluate its thresholds against the un-reconciled 20c reserve rather than ~3c actual — roughly 17c per demo too high, which fires the 50/90/100 percent Sentry alerts early and repeatedly. The test's own title asserts the sequence in prose ('completes the demo, THEN finalizes ... , reports thresholds') while asserting only per-mock call counts. The file already contains the technique that would kill both: the completeDemo step is pinned by holding its promise unresolved (OnboardingDemoWorker.test.ts:253-273) precisely because call-order mocks pass a removed `await`. The same hold, or a mock.invocationCallOrder assertion between mockFinalizeCost and mockCheckCostThreshold, closes this.
findings.reason: CLOSED in 0cf768372. Both round-1 survivors now die against the rewritten success-path test: the block swap FAILS (rt-069) and `await` -> `void` on finalizeOnboardingDemoSpend FAILS (rt-070), because the test holds mockFinalizeCost on a hand-resolved promise and asserts mockCheckCostThreshold has not run at that instant. The pre-existing completeDemo boundary still kills its own mutant (rt-071), and deleting the finalize block fails fast in 1.7s rather than hanging (rt-073). NOTE: the THIRD await in the same block is still unpinned — raised separately as RT-007, not folded into this disposition.

findings.title: Tenant-scope test asserts on SQL source text, so a behaviour-preserving reformat turns it red
findings.reason: REJECTED — the brittleness is deliberate and is the only check of its kind. (1) The behavioural half alone cannot see a rewritten join: `expect(values).toEqual(['demo_123'])` is unchanged by replacing `JOIN accounts a ON a.id = b.account_id` with an unscoped join, so the three `toContain` assertions are the only oracle that detects a re-scoping. (2) A rewrite cannot land silently anyway: scripts/ci/tenant-scope-allowlist.ts:1802-1818 pins the exact SQL snippet in THREE entries for worker/jobs/onboarding-demo/subscription-guard.ts, so `ci:tenant-scope` forces the same change to edit the allowlist in the same PR. (3) A red test on an intentional SQL rewrite is therefore a cheap, correct prompt to re-verify tenant scoping, not a maintenance tax. Verified at HEAD 20087a0cf; no code or test change.

findings.title: The outer catch's failOnboardingDemoTerminal can lose outboxAttempt invisibly — the third instance of the hole D6 and this commit each closed once
findings.arbiter_reasoning: Mutant (inventory rt-079): remove `outboxAttempt,` from the outer-catch `failOnboardingDemoTerminal({...})` call at OnboardingDemoWorker.ts:168-175. Run against the FULL OnboardingDemoWorker.test.ts and stages.test.ts suites together: 38 passed, 0 failed, exit 0. Executed, not an unreached branch — both 'releases reservation when subscription-state failure recording throws' (:190) and 'releases reservation when generic failure recording throws' (:213) drive this exact call site, and each asserts only `expect.objectContaining({ demoId, outboxId, error/failureKind })`, which is satisfied whether or not outboxAttempt is present. Not equivalent: the branch's own docblock (subscription-guard.ts:34-37, mirrored in docs/directory/worker-jobs-c.md) states that forwarding the attempt is load-bearing because failDemo adds `AND attempts = $n` only when it is a number, and that predicate is what stops a stale worker failing a NEWER dispatch. This is the same shape D6 closed on the guard's failTerminal call (asserted with attempt 4 at OnboardingDemoWorker.test.ts:472-477) and that 0cf768372 closed on markOutboxCompleted (attempt 7 at :340-350); the commit message says 'D6 closed exactly this hole on the failDemo side and left its sibling open' — there were two siblings, and this one is still open. The shared harness default returns `attempt: undefined` (OnboardingDemoWorker.test.ts:125), which is precisely why a dropped attempt is indistinguishable. Fix: arm mockExtractOutboxHandle with a nonzero attempt in one of the two failure tests and assert `outboxAttempt` in the objectContaining.
findings.reason: FIXED — verified by mutation at HEAD 20087a0cf. Both forms of the RT-006 mutant now die on `releases exactly once when the generic terminal write fails`: deleting `outboxAttempt,` (rt-080) and `outboxAttempt: undefined` (rt-081). The other two instances of the same hole are independently still closed — the guard call (rt-082) and markOutboxCompleted (rt-083) each die on their own covering test. Three call sites forward an asserted non-zero attempt. NOTE: a FOURTH site exists and is NOT closed — see RT-010.

findings.title: The third awaited boundary in the reworked block is still unpinned: `await` -> `void` on reportOnboardingDemoCostThresholds survives the whole worker suite
findings.arbiter_reasoning: Mutant (inventory rt-072): `await reportOnboardingDemoCostThresholds({` -> `void reportOnboardingDemoCostThresholds({` at OnboardingDemoWorker.ts:155. The covering success-path test PASSES (exit 0), and so does the entire OnboardingDemoWorker.test.ts suite (11 passed, 0 failed). Executed, not an unreached branch — the same test asserts `expect(mockCheckCostThreshold).toHaveBeenCalledTimes(1)`, and the call is issued synchronously by the helper before its first await, so the count assertion holds under the mutant. NOT equivalent, though the difference is narrower than RT-002's: reportOnboardingDemoCostThresholds owns its own try/catch and can never reject, so the mutant cannot change error routing or flip a completed row to failed. What it does change is that handleOnboardingDemo now RESOLVES before the Redis threshold read and the Sentry captureMessage settle — the BullMQ job is acked with the alert still in flight, so on the single-replica worker's graceful shutdown the 50/90/100 alert can be dropped, and `logger.log('... completed ...')` moves ahead of the capture. ARBITER CAVEAT, recorded deliberately: the production code is CORRECT here and no claim on this branch asserts this third boundary — the commit's own comment says 'Hold BOTH awaited boundaries' and both of those now die. This is an oracle gap on an adjacent line, not a defect the fix introduced, and it is a reasonable candidate for the rejection protocol. Fix, if accepted: hold mockCheckCostThreshold on a hand-resolved promise and assert mockLogger.log has not run, exactly as boundaries 1 and 2 do.
findings.reason: FIXED — verified by mutation at HEAD 20087a0cf. `await` -> `void` dies on all three awaited calls in the success block: reportOnboardingDemoCostThresholds (rt-084), finalizeOnboardingDemoSpend (rt-085), completeDemo (rt-086). The now-3-boundary test is neither vacuous nor hang-prone: deleting each awaited call in turn (rt-087/088/089) fails fast in ~2s with the boundary assertion, not a timeout, and the `finally` settles the handler without masking the earlier failure.

findings.title: The RT-003 correction introduced its own unresolvable citation: `60a105d1` is called "the live evidence" but resolves nowhere at HEAD
findings.arbiter_reasoning: Re-resolved at HEAD 0cf768372. The corrected sentence reads "The live evidence is the gate at the rebased HEAD `6c95db21` with fingerprint `60a105d1...`, and it is itself superseded by the post-fix gate recorded in the review report." Measured: `.feature/codex-gate-fingerprint.json` now records headSha 0cf768372ed379402c9094ff95b22bb989b05e38 and fingerprint 7ff1dff74068caa364479623a93c67f0c6a6e391061cd09e5ec2e15c80feb116; `rg -n 60a105d1` over docs/, .claude/reference/ and .feature/ returns ZERO hits outside this red-team report, so a reader cannot resolve the cited fingerprint at all. `6c95db21` does still resolve (it is HEAD~1). The trailing pointer is also dangling: no "review report" records a post-fix gate — the only red-team report on disk is round 1, which itself cites 60a105d1. This is the same class of defect as RT-003 (gate evidence cited at a point the tree has moved past), reproduced one commit later, which is why it is a new P1 rather than a reopening. It is graded P1 and not P0 because the sentence does flag itself as superseded, so a reader is not misled into treating it as current. Fix: cite the live fingerprint 7ff1dff7 at HEAD 0cf768372, or drop the specific values and say only that the gate is re-derived by step 7.5.

The entry now cites NO fingerprint; its two live pointers both resolve: `.agents/skills/feature/scripts/verified-gate.sh` exists and writes `.feature/gate-status.json` (present), and `gate-fingerprint.mjs check` is a real subcommand (gate-fingerprint.mjs:15) that compares the stored hash against the current tree. The superseded `83330f44`/`ce122e52…` and `6c95db21`/`60a105d1…` values survive only as explicitly-labelled history. NO third stale citation was introduced by the fix. Sweep of every SHA/fingerprint/metric claim the branch touched: `6c95db21` and `2870e109…` resolve (`2870e109…` is an ancestor of HEAD, cited as the plan's base, not as current origin/main); `60a105d1` is a fingerprint, not a git object, and is no longer cited as live. The three docs/directory rows check out against code (`createWorkerLogger(prefix, correlationId?)` at logger.ts:189; thresholds `[50, 90, 100]`, levels error/warning/info, tags `lane`+`threshold` at cost-reconcile.ts:56-62). findings.title: The new type predicate narrows nothing any consumer reads — the docblock credits it with a compiler guarantee that no compilation can observe
findings.arbiter_reasoning: The docblock added at OnboardingDemoWorker.ts:48-51 says the predicate exists so 'the `claimed` comment further down is compiler-backed rather than a promise'. Measured two ways at HEAD (inventory rt-078): replacing the whole signature with `function leavesNoWorkToDo(claimResult: ClaimResult): boolean` produced `tsc --noEmit -p tsconfig.json` exit 0 with output byte-identical to the baseline; and narrowing the DECLARED predicate type to `'not_found' | 'already_terminal'` (i.e. making it lie about race_lost) also produced exit 0. Nothing reads `claimResult` after the two `if`s, so the narrowing has no consumer and no compilation outcome depends on it. The claim is true of the type system in the abstract and is not false, but it is unenforced — worth noting on a commit whose stated purpose was striking overstated claims. Also verified while here: the REPLACEMENT claim in the same docblock is correct — adding a sixth member to ClaimResult (src/lib/demos/types.ts:79-84) compiles at exit 0 with zero diagnostics, so the struck 'sixth member is a compile error' claim was rightly struck. P2: informational, no code or doc change required.
findings.reason: FIXED — the new comment is TRUE and both of its claims re-derive at HEAD 20087a0cf. Measured (rt-090): replacing the predicate with `: boolean` leaves `tsc --noEmit -p tsconfig.json` at exit 0 with byte-identical output, so 'NO current caller depends on the narrowing' is exact. The cyclomatic 10 -> 8 claim re-derives by hand (8 with the helper; inlining the three-way `===` chain adds two `||` decision points = 10).

findings.title: The round-2 fix missed a FOURTH outboxAttempt site — the success path's completeDemo attempt is unasserted and `undefined` survives 2666 tests
findings.arbiter_reasoning: Mutant (rt-091): `await completeDemo(sql, 'onboarding_demos', demoId, outboxId, outboxAttempt, {…})` -> `…, outboxId, undefined, {…}`. Run against the whole worker + src/lib/demos sweep: 2666 tests, exit 0, failure set byte-identical to the baseline sweep's 16 pre-existing failures (all Zernio/ingress cases that fail under the scrubbed dotenv env, unrelated to this line). NOT equivalent: completeDemo's 5th parameter is `outboxAttempt: number | undefined` (src/lib/demos/lifecycle.ts:108) and is forwarded verbatim to `markOutboxCompleted(tx, outboxId, outboxAttempt)` (lifecycle.ts:137), which reaches `dispatchedRow(exec, outboxId, attempt)` (src/lib/shared/outbox.ts:106-114) — the attempt is what adds the `AND attempts = $n` CAS predicate, and dropping it lets a stale worker mark a NEWER dispatch completed on the success path. The identical mutation on the sibling call site (rt-083, markOutboxCompleted on the leavesNoWorkToDo path) DIES, which proves the predicate is load-bearing and the difference is purely oracle coverage. NOT an unexecuted branch: the success-path test asserts completeDemo was called. ROOT CAUSE, same as RT-006: the only covering test asserts `toHaveBeenCalledWith(mockSql, 'onboarding_demos', 'demo_123', 'outbox-demo-1', undefined, {…})` — a literal `undefined` supplied by the shared harness default `extractOutboxHandle -> { attempt: undefined }` (OnboardingDemoWorker.test.ts:117-123), so the asserted value is indistinguishable from a dropped one. This also falsifies the fix commit's own claims that 'this is the last of the three' and 'Every authority-bearing argument on this lane is now asserted explicitly'. FIX: in the success-path test, override `mockExtractOutboxHandle.mockReturnValueOnce({ outboxId: 'outbox_from_payload', attempt: N })` with a non-zero N and assert that N as completeDemo's 5th argument — exactly the shape rt-080/082/083 already use.

authorizations.text:
Question: Red-team round 2's fixes moved HEAD, so its sidecar is stale and still reads OPEN_P0. Authorize a third round to re-verify mechanically? The option offered and chosen was: 'Authorize round 3 — the mechanism the checker documents for exactly this case. A scoped round re-mutates only the RT-006/007 fix hunks, resolves dispositions from real evidence, and recomputes status. Costs one more agent pass; it is the only path that clears OPEN_P0 honestly.' The two alternatives offered were recording the P0s as accepted-risk, and stopping at review with OPEN_P0 on record.
Owner: Authorize round 3 (Recommended)
